remaining_gaps: Section 7 (Postal Service) ends by its own terms "until changed by the Postal Service in accordance with the Postal Reorganization Act"; no packet source records whether or when the Postal Service changed the order's application to its employees. Missing: the Postal Service holiday-observance regulation or national agreement provision that replaced the order for postal employees, with its date and a held text.

Section 2(a) lists the fourth Monday of October as a holiday; the held 5 U.S.C. 6103 text (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s6103.txt, not a registered packet source) lists Veterans Day on November 11, so that list entry was displaced by statute. Missing: Pub. L. 94-97 (or the Code history) as a registered packet source, and a source deciding whether the rest of the section 2(a) definition continues.

Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 (substitute workdays when a holiday falls on Sunday or a non-workday) overlap 5 U.S.C. 6103(b); whether any command was extinguished by the statute is unresolved because the statute text is held only outside the packet catalogue.

The only registered current-law record (CURRENT:EO:11582#0, the 5 U.S.C. 6103 note) cannot be quote-verified by the claim checker (it reads USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl as raw JSON lines), and 5 CFR 610.201 and 610.202 (which cite the order) are held outside the packet catalogue.

Inventory defects need correction before a claim: the dossier has no clause for section 1 (OCR "Section h") or section 5 (OCR "Sec. 5,"; its text sits inside section 4(d)), and section 3(a) is merged into section 3.

Section 1 of the order delegates about 50 separate presidential functions, each under its own statute (for example 5 U.S.C. 5514, 5702, 5742, 5911, 5942, 5942a and 5943; 7 U.S.C. 1011 and 1990; 10 U.S.C. 126, 1074 and 1085; 16 U.S.C. 831c and 831f; 20 U.S.C. 191 and 905; 22 U.S.C. 287e-1 and 2679). The packet holds the current text of none of these statutes and only two current-law records (the 3 U.S.C. 301 note and the 38 U.S.C. 111 note), so no paragraph other than those can be shown to rest on a statute still in force on 2026-10-14. Missing: the current text of each delegated statute, or a held current record for each paragraph.

Later instruments touching the order whose provisions the packet did not locate: Executive Order 11429 (September 9, 1968, cross-referenced), Executive Order 12107 (December 28, 1978) and Executive Order 12608 (September 9, 1987). Their provisions on Executive Order 11609 must be read and attached before any clause can be called unamended.

Paragraphs (22) and (23) of section 1 were revoked by Executive Order 12215 section 1-404 (May 27, 1980), which also revoked Executive Order 11713 that added them; section 4 was amended by Executive Order 11779 (April 19, 1974), subsection 7 by Executive Order 12466 (February 27, 1984) and Executive Order 12522 (June 24, 1985), and section 8 by Executive Order 12822 (November 16, 1992). A claim would need a per-paragraph state for every one of them with the before-and-after wording.

Inventory defects: the dossier has a duplicate-scope clause (sec1-b-dup2), no clause for section 7, and about 61 clauses whose spans were not checked against the original; a corrected inventory with new spans is required.
